topic: The Pi-Collision Paradox: Why Bouncing Blocks Count Digits of Pi
target_audience: University students (Physics/Math) or curious high schoolers

sections.title: The Hook: A Counter-Intuitive Puzzle
lecture_lines: A small block bounces between a wall and a big block.
Surprisingly, the answer relates to Pi.
animations: Show a small block moving toward a larger block. Color: #FFFFFF.
Flash the small block as it collides with the wall. Color: #FF0000.
Display the symbol 'Pi' next to the blocks. Color: #00FF00.

sections.title: Prerequisite Physics: Conservation Laws
lecture_lines: Collisions must conserve total momentum and energy.
Massive blocks act like moving walls.
Small blocks are forced to reverse direction.
animations: Display momentum conservation formula: p1+p2=const. Color: #FFFFFF.
Animate big block moving as a wall. Color: #FFFF00.

sections.title: Mapping Physics to Geometry: The Phase Space
lecture_lines: View each collision as a reflection.
The path length equals the arc.
animations: Draw an arc over the path. Color: #FF00FF.

sections.title: The Connection to Pi
lecture_lines: Mass ratio controls the wedge angle.
The count reveals digits of Pi.
animations: Add reflections to the wedge. Color: #FFFF00.

sections.title: Conclusion and Intuition
lecture_lines: Physics and math are deeply linked.
animations: Connect physics and math labels. Color: #00FFFF.
